subject: chemistry
title: Naming and formulae of organic compounds
key_idea: A **hydrocarbon** contains carbon and hydrogen only. Organic compounds are grouped into **homologous series**, each with a **functional group** that decides its reactions. A systematic name is built from the longest carbon chain, the functional group and the side groups.

blocks.text: Organic compounds fall into families. This section covers the key terms used to describe a family and the molecules in it.

items.meaning: A compound made of carbon and hydrogen atoms only.
A family of compounds with the same functional group, in which each member differs from the next by CH₂.
The atom or group of atoms that is responsible for the characteristic reactions of a compound.
The simplest algebraic formula for any member of a homologous series, such as CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes.
An alkane with one hydrogen removed, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁. It is written R when its identity does not matter.

items: Members of a series have **similar chemical properties**, because they share a functional group.
Physical properties change gradually along the series, for example boiling point rises as the chain gets longer.
The functional group decides how a molecule reacts. The rest of the molecule is mostly unreactive.
Carbon skeletons can be straight chains, branched chains or rings (cyclic).

rows: C–C and C–H single bonds only

items: A hydrocarbon has carbon and hydrogen only.
A homologous series has one functional group, and each member differs by CH₂.
The functional group decides the chemical properties.

blocks.text: One molecule can be shown in six ways. Each gives a different amount of detail, and the examples below use butan-2-ol.

rows: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element
The actual number of atoms of each element
An algebraic formula for the whole series
The minimum detail needed to show how the atoms are arranged
Every atom and every bond drawn out
All C–H, C–C, C–O and O–H bonds drawn
Carbon chain as a zig-zag with hydrogens on carbon left out; functional groups shown
A zig-zag of four carbons with OH on the second

items: In a **skeletal formula** each corner and each line end is a carbon atom. Hydrogens on carbon are not drawn.
Atoms other than carbon and hydrogen are always drawn, as are hydrogens in a functional group such as O–H.
A **displayed formula** shows the bond between every pair of atoms, including each C–H bond.
A ring is drawn as a polygon. Cyclohexane is a plain hexagon.

blocks.label: General formula of an alkane
where: n, the number of carbon atoms

items.text: An alkane with 7 carbon atoms has n = 7.

diagram.alt: A practice question: use the general formula of an alkane to find the number of hydrogen atoms.
diagram.question: An alkane has {n} carbon atoms. How many hydrogen atoms are in one molecule?
working: The general formula of an alkane is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

items: Empirical formula is the simplest ratio. Molecular formula is the actual number of atoms.
Structural shows the arrangement, displayed shows every bond, skeletal shows the carbon chain only.
Put n into a general formula to get the molecular formula of any member.

blocks.text: IUPAC names follow fixed rules, so every compound has one unambiguous name. Learn the stems first, then the order of the rules.

items.text: that contains the functional group. This gives the stem.
with a suffix such as -ol, -al, -one, -oic acid or -ene, or a prefix such as chloro- or bromo-.
from the end that gives the functional group the lowest number.
as an alkyl group or halogen, with the number of the carbon it is on.
Side groups go first in alphabetical order. Use di-, tri- or tetra- for repeats, and commas between numbers.

items: CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂OH is **2-methylbutan-1-ol**. The chain has four carbons, the –OH is on carbon 1 and a methyl group is on carbon 2.
CH₃CHBrCH₃ is **2-bromopropane**. The bromine is on the middle carbon.
A ring takes the prefix cyclo-, as in cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂).
Numbers are separated from letters by hyphens, and numbers from each other by commas, as in 2,3-dimethylpentane.
Learn the stems meth- to dec-.
The longest chain with the functional group gives the stem, and the numbering gives the functional group the lowest number.
Side groups are listed alphabetically before the stem.

checks.q: Give the molecular formula of the alkane with 12 carbon atoms.
Name CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH, and state what its skeletal formula would show.
checks.a: 3-methylbutan-1-ol. The skeletal formula is a zig-zag of four carbons with OH at one end and a methyl branch on the third carbon, with no hydrogens on carbon drawn.

checks.q: Explain what is meant by a homologous series, and why its members have similar chemical properties.
checks.a: A family of compounds with the same functional group, where each member differs from the next by CH₂. They have similar chemical properties because the functional group is responsible for the reactions.

blocks.text: Hydrocarbons and their rings and chains are described with extra terms, and the saturated or unsaturated nature of a molecule matters.

items.meaning: A compound of carbon and hydrogen joined in straight chains, branched chains or non-aromatic rings.
An aliphatic compound arranged in non-aromatic rings, with or without side chains.
A compound that contains a benzene ring.
Having multiple carbon–carbon bonds, including C=C, C≡C and aromatic rings.

items: Benzene is drawn as a hexagon with an inner circle, or as a hexagon with alternating double bonds.
In a structural formula the carboxyl group is written COOH and the ester group COO.
R represents an alkyl group, or any other part of a molecule that does not take part in the reaction.

blocks.text: You must be able to go in both directions between a name and a structure.

items: Draw structural, displayed and skeletal formulae for a given compound.
Name a compound from its structure, for chains and rings of up to six carbon atoms.
Draw the structure of a compound from its name, with the same limit of six carbon atoms in a chain or ring.

blocks.text: The nomenclature you need is limited, and the way a molecule is built is described with set words.

items: Name simple aliphatic compounds with up to six carbon atoms.
Esters and amides may have six carbons on each side of the –COO– or amide link, but their chains are straight only. Nitriles are also straight chains only.
Rings with a single ring of up to six carbon atoms can be named.
Describe a molecule as straight-chained, branched or cyclic.
